title: Undecidable quantum storage with seven elementary gates
description: Can one decide from its noise rate whether a fixed local quantum medium is an excellent memory or no scalable memory at all? We construct two six-dimensional media, one for whole-site and one for independent single-qubit depolarization, for which this distinction is undecidable. Both circuits use only X, H, CNOT, Toffoli, reset, dephasing and identity, with noise after every elementary layer. Computable disjoint rational windows select universal-machine inputs. For every nonhalting input and all sizes above a computable threshold, one total computable encoder preserves a reference-entangled qubit with fidelity at least 15/16 through an exponential number of rounds, uniformly across its window. On halting windows every encoding into the entire physical algebra fails after a time uniform in size and rate. A capped static computational chart and a protected finite counter permit exponential operation; complete source witnesses control correlated controller errors on the torus. For these media we give a coarse lifetime upper bound exponential in the fourth power of size and Π⁰₁-complete certification by exact finite tests. The three-dimensional construction retains its sharp linear storage scale. The interactions have fixed finite range and astronomical constants. Every finite sample eventually forgets; what is undecidable is how its useful storage time grows with size.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 2.0.0 updates version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24254846). New: Theorem B, exponential qubit storage on the undecidable noise windows for fixed seven-gate media on Z^6, under whole-site and under single-qubit depolarization after every layer, with every-encoding destruction on halting windows; Proposition 9.8, a coarse exp(O_n(L^4)) lifetime upper bound and Pi^0_1-complete certification. Theorem A (Z^3, sharp linear storage) is unchanged. The authors have not independently verified the mathematical arguments; the work used a combination of AI models with cross-developer checks.
